description:
FILED s433 (Fable review probe while ruling #456 half (b); PRE-EXISTING).  THE GENERAL FORM of #456 half (b): closes together with it (plan-post-s433 Q3).

A BEGIN block in a LATER package section runs AFTER an EARLIER section's run-time statements:

    our $x = 5;
    { package Q; sub q1 { 1 } }
    BEGIN { print "B=[$main::x]\n" }
    print "end\n";
        perl: B=[]  end      (BEGIN runs at compile time, before the assignment)
        PCL:  B=[5] end      <- SILENT WRONG

The single-section inverse is RIGHT (`our $x = 5; BEGIN { print "B=[$main::x]\n" }` -> B=[] under both) -- so the bug is exactly that section 1's RUN forms are emitted before section 2's compile-phase forms (Parser2's section assembly emits decls/captured/defs/sched/run per section, sections in sequence).  #456's `{ package Q; print main::nm() } sub nm {"PKG"}` is the same bug seen through a sub definition.

RULED SHAPE (fable-answers-s433 Â§B.4): perl's PHASE model across sections -- emit every section's compile-phase forms (decls, captured, defs, sched; source order kept) before any section's run-phase forms, each group under its own (in-package ...) switches.  MOVE, never copy.  NEVER "hoist the definition alone": a sub body above its own section's decls compiles a p-defcell SYMBOL-MACRO (`main::$x`) as a plain free variable -- probed s433 on `my $x = 5; { package Q; print main::nm() } sub nm { $x }`, whose body emits as (block nil main::$x) with the cell defined in its section's decls.  Fallback if the two-phase A/B shows an unexplainable diff class: on-demand hoist of the needed section's decls+defs.

MEASURE FIRST: what the five section lists hold; how many files are multi-section (the on-demand stub count is 75 of 722; the phase model moves every multi-section file's ORDER); whether any `sched` form is entitled to an earlier section's run-time state (perl: no); compile time.

BAR: this reproducer + #456's + the inverses (single-section BEGIN, same-section call, sub-first, no-package-switch) vs perl; four-population A/B with every diff explained (expected class: ordering only); full sweep TOTAL/LOST; companion on the #467 runner; gate; generation bump + the three artifacts; docs/ir-spec.md load-model line ("compile phase precedes run phase across sections"); sort.t's bug-36430 row returns to pass-baseline by EDIT; the two Pl/t/decl-ordering-02.t #456 guard rows become one both_agree.


=== DONE s436 (Opus 5), commit b95ad91; #456 half (b) closes with it.

THE SHAPE, as ruled: two passes over @sections in Pl::Parser2::parse â every
section's compile phase (package preamble + decls + version defvar + $a/$b +
forward globals + captured + the defs/sched interleave, source order kept
within and across sections), then `(p-run-compile-phase-blocks)` once, then
every section's run phase.  Nothing compiled twice; the forms MOVE.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT ADDED TO THE DESIGN, and it is the part worth re-reading:

 1. A run group needs an `(in-package â¦)`.  in-package is READ-time and pass 1
    leaves the reader in the LAST section's package.  Tracked with a $reader
    variable so a ONE-section file emits nothing new and stays byte-identical.

 2. `p-BEGIN` SETS the runtime current package on entry and NEVER RESTORES it
    (now #474).  Invisible before, because a section's BEGINs ran immediately
    before that same section's run forms.  Under the phase model the package
    left current when the run phase starts is the LAST BEGIN's -- measured:
    perl-tests/caller.t 15 -> 13, because `{ package RT129239; BEGIN {â¦} }` at
    line 369 made the `eval 'pb()'` at line 129 transpile in RT129239 and
    answer undef.  FIXED by making every run group state its own package
    (section 0 included) whenever the file has more than one section.

 3. `@ver_run` (the `package Foo 1.5;` $VERSION assignment) went to the END of
    its section's COMPILE phase -- perl sets it at compile time, and that keeps
    it where it always was relative to the phase boundary and to every run
    form.  UNMEASURED: no file in any of the four populations uses that
    spelling (t/comp/package_block.t does and fails identically either way).

 4. The on-demand cross-section p-declare-sub stub block was left UNTOUCHED.
    It is now partly redundant (an earlier section's RUN-TIME call no longer
    needs a stub), but it still serves an earlier section's BEGIN, and
    narrowing it would have added a diff class to this change.

BAR, all met: four-population A/B with a LINE-MULTISET walker -- 344 changed
files, ZERO removed lines, every added line an (in-package â¦) or a
(p-set-current-package â¦); sweep TOTAL 18311 -> 18312 (+1 = sort.t's bug-36430
row, back for real) GATE clean; companion NET +36 C_ok over five files
(op/gmagic.t 4 -> 30) with nothing lost, each gainer attributed on a base
worktree; gate 163/5739; generation v2-180 + three artifacts; ir-spec Â§9 load
model; six both_agree guard rows in decl-ordering-02.t; a STALE guard in
begin-end-01.t that was encoding the bug, repaired in the same commit.
subject: Cross-section PHASE order: a BEGIN (or sub def) in a LATER package section runs after an EARLIER section's run-time statements -- the general form of #456 half (b); emit compile-phase forms of all sections first
